reader.requirement: At 1985 an arithmetic statement with multiple results must first access every item of its initial evaluation, compute that once into a temporary, before any resultant is stored, for ADD/SUBTRACT/MULTIPLY/DIVIDE in-place and GIVING forms and COMPUTE; the witnesses cover ADD TO, MULTIPLY BY, COMPUTE and DIVIDE REMAINDER but not SUBTRACT FROM, DIVIDE INTO, or GIVING forms of ADD/SUBTRACT/MULTIPLY/DIVIDE with aliasing receivers.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal: 1985 wraps an unphrased statement in the catch-every-condition two-phase shape; the initial-evaluation snapshot and the per-receiver loop inside are the same code

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|DialectBehaviors|EditionContext|CobolVersion over ArithmeticEmitter.cs, ReceiverBracketEmitter.cs, SendingValueTemp.cs, ExpressionBinder.cs#ResolveReceivingAtStore: no edition test governs the snapshot or the receiver order
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the probe prints identical lines at --std 85 and --std 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: SUBTRACT FROM, DIVIDE INTO and the GIVING forms of ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY and DIVIDE with a receiver that aliases an operand are not exercised

probes.expected: one temporary per statement (X=6, Y=9): SUBTRACT X Y FROM X Z -> -9, -15; DIVIDE X INTO X Y -> 1, 1.5; GIVING X Y Z forms all store the value of the senders before the first store
ADD 1 TO N, OE (N) with OE OCCURS DEPENDING ON N: temp 1, N=3, OE(3)=2
ADD 5 TO S1 S2 S3 with S1 PIC 9 overflowing (no phrase, 1985: S1 undefined) leaves the other receivers stored from the one temp

probes.printed: COBOL0001 at EQUAL (COMPUTE X Y EQUAL 3); COBOL1689 for literal receiver in ADD 1 TO X 5; COBOL0803 ROUNDED MODE IS requires COBOL-2014
probes.expected: refusals at 85: EQUAL in COMPUTE and ROUNDED MODE are later-edition forms; a literal is not a resultant

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.4.6 GR1  (6.4.6 Multiple Results in Arithmetic Statements)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: Each arithmetic emitter evaluates the senders once and Snapshots them into a local before the receiver loop whenever there is more than one receiver or a run-time-identified receiver, so aliasing receivers cannot change the stored value. Probes over every verb's multiple-receiver forms at --std 85 gave the one-temporary result; --std 2023 prints the same.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.6.6.4 GR1-2 and VI.6.11.4 GR1 (1985 DIVIDE format 1 stores identifier-1 in the temporary). refute-1985-022/r2multb-001 at --std 85, forms the reader did not try: ADD I TO T (I), I with I=2 -> T(2)=3, I=4 (temp taken from I before I is stored); COMPUTE I, T (I) = I + 1 -> I=3, T(3)=3; MULTIPLY 1.5 BY I ROUNDED, T (I) (I=3) -> I=5, T(5)=3; MULTIPLY AA (I) BY I, AA (I) ON SIZE ERROR with I overflowing -> I=3 kept, AA(3)=25 from the one temp; r2mfix2-001 ADD I K TO K, T (K), I (I=2,K=1) -> K=4, T(4)=4, I=5. Class b/c: r2ref-001 ADD T (I) TO I, T (I) GIVING K refused COBOL1689 (1985 format 2 has one operand after TO), r2mfix-001 SUBTRACT I FROM K, T (K), I GIVING I refused COBOL1689. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.6.4.6 GR1  (6.4.6 Multiple Results in Arithmetic Statements)  the text is in GR1
